definition: Dividing one large network into smaller networks to organize and secure traffic.
exampleSentence: Subnetting lets us give each department its own small network with a clear address range.

definition: A list of rules that tells a router where to send each packet.
exampleSentence: I checked the routing table and found that no route existed for the new office network.

definition: A network device that connects computers in the same local network.
exampleSentence: The cable from the printer is plugged into the wrong port on the switch.

definition: When some data packets never reach their destination.
exampleSentence: Video calls freeze because the Wi-Fi in that room has serious packet loss.

definition: Recording the real network traffic so that it can be analyzed later.
exampleSentence: We ran a packet capture on the server to see why the connection kept resetting.

definition: Spreading incoming requests across several servers so that none is overloaded.
exampleSentence: Load balancing keeps the website fast even when thousands of users arrive at once.

definition: A server that receives requests from the internet and passes them to internal servers.
exampleSentence: A reverse proxy in front of the application handles HTTPS and hides the real servers.

definition: A security model that never trusts a user or device automatically, even inside the network.
exampleSentence: With zero trust, every request must prove who it is, even from the office network.

definition: Splitting a network into zones so an attack cannot spread easily.
exampleSentence: Network segmentation stopped the malware from moving from the guest Wi-Fi to the servers.

definition: A protocol that uses encrypted tickets to prove identity inside a company network.
exampleSentence: Users log in once and Kerberos gives them tickets to open file shares without typing a password again.

definition: A special account used by an application or script instead of a real person.
exampleSentence: The backup job runs under a service account that has no permission to sign in interactively.

definition: Rules that allow or block sign-in depending on the user, device or location.
exampleSentence: Conditional access asks for extra verification when someone logs in from another country.

definition: A service that stores user identities and confirms them for other applications.
exampleSentence: Our identity provider confirms who you are, so each app does not need its own password.

definition: Software that creates and runs virtual machines on a physical server.
exampleSentence: We installed a hypervisor on the new server to run ten virtual machines on it.

definition: A saved copy of a system's state that you can return to later.
exampleSentence: Take a snapshot of the virtual machine before you install the update.

definition: A design that keeps a service running even when one component fails.
exampleSentence: The database uses high availability, so a second server takes over if the first one crashes.

definition: The automatic switch to a backup system when the main one fails.
exampleSentence: During the outage, failover moved all traffic to the second data center in under a minute.

definition: A group of servers that work together as one system.
exampleSentence: The application runs on a cluster of five servers so it never depends on a single machine.

definition: The plan and tools used to restore systems after a major failure.
exampleSentence: Our disaster recovery plan says we must restore the main systems within four hours.

definition: Keeping the most important business activities running during a crisis.
exampleSentence: Business continuity planning helped us keep serving customers while the office was closed.

definition: Keeping the settings of servers consistent and tracked in a controlled way.
exampleSentence: Configuration management makes sure every web server has exactly the same settings.

definition: Describing servers and networks in code files so they can be created automatically.
exampleSentence: We describe our whole network with Infrastructure as Code and store it in Git.

definition: The process of planning, testing and installing software updates on all systems.
exampleSentence: Good patch management means no server stays unpatched for more than two weeks.

definition: A prepared, approved system copy used to set up new computers quickly.
exampleSentence: New laptops are installed from the golden image, so every employee starts with the same software.

definition: Estimating how many resources you will need so systems do not run out.
exampleSentence: Capacity planning showed that we need more storage before the end of the year.

definition: The normal level of performance used to notice when something changes.
exampleSentence: Our monitoring tool learns the baseline and warns us when traffic is far above it.

definition: Actively searching a network for hidden attackers instead of waiting for alerts.
exampleSentence: The team spends every Friday on threat hunting to look for signs that tools may have missed.

definition: An authorized attack on your own systems to find weaknesses before real hackers do.
exampleSentence: We hired an outside company to run penetration testing on our new customer portal.

definition: When an attacker moves from one compromised machine to others inside a network.
exampleSentence: The logs showed lateral movement from a reception computer to the finance server.

definition: Gaining higher permissions than you were given, often by exploiting a bug.
exampleSentence: The attacker used a bug to perform privilege escalation and became an administrator.

definition: A security flaw that attackers use before the vendor knows about it or has a fix.
exampleSentence: Nobody had a patch yet, because the attack used a zero-day in the browser.

definition: Reducing a system's attack surface by turning off unneeded features and tightening settings.
exampleSentence: Server hardening includes closing unused ports and removing default accounts.

definition: Collecting and analyzing digital evidence to understand what happened in an incident.
exampleSentence: Forensics showed that the attacker first entered through a forgotten test server.

definition: A record of who handled digital evidence so that it can be trusted.
exampleSentence: We documented every step in the chain of custody before giving the disk to the lawyers.

definition: The unauthorized copying or sending of data out of an organization.
exampleSentence: Unusual uploads at night were the first sign of data exfiltration from the file server.

definition: Giving users and programs only the access they need to do their job.
exampleSentence: Following the principle of least privilege, interns can read the documents but cannot delete them.

definition: A secured server that admins must pass through to reach other internal systems.
exampleSentence: You must connect to the jump host first, then open an SSH session to the database.

definition: A hardened server that is the only public entry point into a private network.
exampleSentence: Only the bastion host accepts connections from the internet, and every login on it is logged.

definition: Keeping a system completely disconnected from other networks, including the internet.
exampleSentence: The most sensitive backups are stored on an air gap system that no hacker can reach remotely.

definition: A fake system built to attract attackers so that the team can study their methods.
exampleSentence: The honeypot looked like a real server, and it caught three scanning attempts in one day.
